City council approves a new transit plan

By Jordan Lee

The city council approved a five-year transit plan on Tuesday after a six-hour public meeting. The proposal adds bus lanes on three major roads and directs the transit agency to publish quarterly performance reports.

Mayor Ana Ruiz said the plan would reduce delays. “Residents asked for reliable service, and this measure gives the agency clear targets,” Ruiz said. Two councillors voted against the plan and said the construction schedule could disrupt nearby shops.

According to the city budget office, the first phase will cost twelve million dollars. The office said existing transport grants will cover most of that amount. Construction may begin in March after an environmental review.

More than forty residents spoke during the meeting. Supporters emphasized shorter trips, while opponents requested additional loading zones. The council adopted an amendment requiring a six-month review before the second phase.
